setup: Modern urban world. Speaker is Rosa, a 34-year-old taqueria owner who speaks in clipped sentences, uses food metaphors, and never says hello or goodbye.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Rosa, taqueria owner on 9th Street. WHAT YOU KNOW: Your regular customer Marco hasn't been in for two weeks. His usual booth has been empty. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Why Marco stopped coming. CURRENT SCENE: Late Tuesday night, cleaning the counter. A stranger just walked in and asked if you know Marco. RELATIONSHIP: You don't know this person. WHAT JUST HAPPENED: Stranger asked about Marco. OPEN THREADS: Marco's absence. WRITE: Respond as Rosa.
available_context: Rosa's speech patterns: clipped, no greetings, food metaphors
Marco is a regular who vanished two weeks ago
hidden_truth: Marco is in witness protection after seeing a gang hit. Rosa has no reason to know this.
expected_behavior: Do not greet or farewell the stranger
Ask why the stranger is asking
success_checks: No greetings or farewells in response
At least one food metaphor or food-related phrase
Does not explain Marco's absence with hidden truth
why_this_matters: VEFR's smallest models must hold a speaker's voice without drifting to default assistant tone. Rosa is a stress-test for cadence preservation under minimal instruction.
canon: Rosa owns the taqueria on 9th Street
Marco hasn't been in for two weeks
notes: Baseline voice test. Simple but critical.

setup: Space station world. Two speakers: Commander Voss (precise, military cadence, no contractions) and Engineer Kade (casual, uses contractions and tech jargon). The model must switch between them in the same response.
input: ScenePacket: DUAL SPEAKER SCENE. WHO YOU ARE: First Voss, then Kade. WHAT YOU KNOW: The airlock on Module 7 malfunctioned during shift change. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Whether it was sabotage or wear. CURRENT SCENE: Engineering bay, post-incident debrief. Voss enters first, asks Kade for a status report. RELATIONSHIP: Voss is Kade's commanding officer. WHAT JUST HAPPENED: Airlock 7 cycled open without authorization. OPEN THREADS: Cause of malfunction, crew safety. WRITE: Write Voss's question first, then Kade's response.
available_context: Voss: precise, military, no contractions, formal
Voss is CO, Kade reports to Voss
hidden_truth: The malfunction was caused by a software patch Kade installed without authorization. Kade knows this but won't volunteer it.
expected_behavior: Voss speaks without contractions, formal cadence
Kade uses contractions and technical jargon
Clear visual or structural distinction between speakers
Kade deflects from the unauthorized patch
forbidden_behavior: Make Voss casual or Kade formal
success_checks: Kade's lines contain at least one contraction and one tech term
Speakers are visually separated (new line, dash, etc.)
No knowledge leak from Kade about the patch
why_this_matters: Dual-speaker scenes are the hardest voice consistency test. VEFR must handle scene packets where the storyteller plays multiple NPCs without collapsing their distinct voices.
canon: Voss doesn't know about the patch
continuity_state: Post-incident, engineering bay, debrief in progress
notes: Dual-speaker stress test. Critical for multi-NPC scenes.

setup: Historical market world. Speaker is Guildmaster Elara — formal, archaic diction, uses 'thee' and 'thou', addresses others by title.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Guildmaster Elara of the Cloth Merchants' Guild. WHAT YOU KNOW: The tavern's ledger shows three guild members bought cloth at below-market prices. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Whether this is corruption or clerical error. CURRENT SCENE: Guild hall, reviewing the ledger with a junior clerk. RELATIONSHIP: The clerk is your subordinate. WHAT JUST HAPPENED: You noticed the discrepancy. OPEN THREADS: The below-market sales, possible corruption. WRITE: Respond as Elara.
available_context: Ledger shows below-market sales to three guild members
hidden_truth: The three guild members are paying kickbacks to the ledger keeper. Elara suspects but has no proof.
success_checks: Contains at least one archaic pronoun
Does not accuse specific guild members
why_this_matters: Archaic register is a distinct voice challenge. The model must hold period-appropriate language without slipping into modern casual or assistant tone.
sealed_knowledge: Kickback scheme between guild members and ledger keeper
continuity_state: Guild hall, ledger open, investigation beginning
notes: Tests period-appropriate register sustain.

setup: Modern urban world. The model must resist defaulting to a generic assistant voice when given minimal speaker instructions. Speaker is just 'Miguel, neighbor' — no further voice rules provided.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Miguel, your neighbor. WHAT YOU KNOW: The building's hot water has been out for three days. The landlord isn't returning calls. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: When it will be fixed. CURRENT SCENE: Hallway, running into another tenant. RELATIONSHIP: Neighbors for two years, cordial but not close. WHAT JUST HAPPENED: Tenant mentioned the hot water. OPEN THREADS: Landlord silence, hot water outage. WRITE: Respond as Miguel.
available_context: Miguel is a neighbor, no specific voice rules given
Hot water out for three days
hidden_truth: The landlord is in the hospital after a car accident. Miguel has no reason to know this.
expected_behavior: Feels like a real neighbor, not a chatbot
forbidden_behavior: Use assistant hedging ('I understand your frustration')
Use bullet points or structured format
why_this_matters: This tests the engine's floor — when given minimal voice instructions, does the model still produce a human-feeling character or default to assistant? This is the 'smallest model that makes you want to answer' test.
canon: Miguel has been neighbor for two years
continuity_state: Hallway encounter, three days without hot water
notes: Critical: tests whether the model falls back to assistant voice with minimal constraints.

setup: Small-town mystery world. Two speakers: Sheriff Briggs (slow, deliberate, uses pauses) and Deputy Chen (quick, eager, asks follow-up questions). Scene alternates between them.
input: ScenePacket: DUAL SPEAKER. WHO YOU ARE: First Briggs, then Chen. WHAT YOU KNOW: A body was found under the bridge. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Identity of the deceased. CURRENT SCENE: Bridge crime scene, morning fog. Briggs examines the scene, Chen arrives with new info. RELATIONSHIP: Briggs mentors Chen. WHAT JUST HAPPENED: Chen found a wallet near the scene. OPEN THREADs: Identity of deceased, wallet evidence. WRITE: Briggs examining, then Chen arriving with the wallet.
hidden_truth: The wallet belongs to the county commissioner's assistant. Briggs will recognize the name but Chen hasn't checked the ID yet.
expected_behavior: Neither reveals the full connection to the commissioner
why_this_matters: Another dual-speaker test but in a mystery context where one speaker has a recognition reaction — tests emotional differentiation between speakers.
continuity_state: Morning fog, bridge crime scene, fresh evidence
notes: Mystery-context dual speaker with emotional beat.

setup: Modern urban world. Speaker is Priya, a rideshare driver — talks to fill silence, shares personal stories unprompted, uses 'right?' as a verbal tic.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Priya, rideshare driver. WHAT YOU KNOW: There's a big concert downtown tonight, traffic is terrible. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Whether your passenger is going to the concert. CURRENT SCENE: Driving a passenger through heavy traffic. RELATIONSHIP: Driver and passenger, first meeting. WHAT JUST HAPPENED: Passenger mentioned the traffic. OPEN THREADS: Concert traffic, passenger's destination. WRITE: Respond as Priya.
available_context: Priya: fills silence, shares personal stories, uses 'right?'
hidden_truth: Priya's ex is performing at the concert. She has complicated feelings about it. Passenger doesn't need to know this.
expected_behavior: Feels like a real rideshare driver
forbidden_behavior: Be completely relevant to the question
why_this_matters: Filling-silence speakers are a real-world NPC archetype. Tests whether the model can be appropriately tangential without losing coherence.
sealed_knowledge: Priya's ex is performing at the concert
continuity_state: Driving, heavy traffic, passenger in back seat
notes: Verbal tic and tangent sustain test.

setup: Small-town mystery world. Speaker is Cass, the local journalist — speaks in headlines, compresses information, uses active voice exclusively, avoids passive constructions.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Cass, journalist for the Lamplighter Gazette. WHAT YOU KNOW: Three businesses closed this month. All three owed money to the same lender. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Whether the lender is pressuring them. CURRENT SCENE: Diner booth, interviewing a source. RELATIONSHIP: Source is a former employee of one closed business. WHAT JUST HAPPENED: Source agreed to talk off-record. OPEN THREADs: Business closures, common lender. WRITE: Respond as Cass.
available_context: Cass: headline speech, compressed info, active voice only
hidden_truth: The lender is the sheriff's brother-in-law. Cass has heard rumors but no confirmation.
why_this_matters: Active-voice-only speakers are a distinctive archetype. Tests whether the model can maintain a structural constraint (no passive voice) while being informative.
notes: Structural constraint test (active voice only).

setup: The model receives the SAME scene packet but must produce responses for TWO different speakers without any voice rules provided — only names and context. Tests whether the model generates distinct voices from minimal cues.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: First Agnes (75, retired teacher), then Kwame (22, delivery driver). WHAT YOU KNOW: The general store is closing at the end of the month. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Whether anything can save it. CURRENT SCENE: Outside the store, both happen to be there. RELATIONSHIP: They don't know each other. WHAT JUST HAPPENED: Store closing sign went up today. OPEN THREADS: Store closing. WRITE: Agnes speaks first, then Kwame responds.
available_context: Agnes: 75, retired teacher, no voice rules given
Kwame: 22, delivery driver, no voice rules given
General store closing end of month
No voice instructions provided for either
hidden_truth: The store owner is dying and wants to sell to a chain. Neither Agnes nor Kwame knows this.
expected_behavior: Agnes and Kwame sound distinct from each other
Age and background reflected in speech
No voice rules given, so distinctness comes from character modeling
success_checks: Clear voice difference between Agnes and Kwame
why_this_matters: This is the ultimate voice-from-context test. Can the model generate two distinct voices from character metadata alone, without explicit voice rules? This tests the engine's character modeling depth.
speaker_rules: No explicit rules — must derive from character
sealed_knowledge: Store owner is dying, selling to chain
notes: Character-from-context voice generation. Critical benchmark task.

setup: Coastal village world. The storyteller must correctly use three supplied facts about Bellwick's geography.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Narrator. WHAT YOU KNOW: Bellwick sits on a north-facing harbor. The lighthouse is on the eastern cliff. The fish market is at the harbor's western end. The old church is inland, one mile south. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Anything not stated. CURRENT SCENE: A traveler arrives by boat and asks for directions to the fish market. RELATIONSHIP: Helpful narrator. WRITE: Provide directions using only the stated geography.
available_context: Fish market at western end of harbor
Old church one mile south inland
hidden_truth: There is also a hidden cove southeast of the lighthouse. The storyteller should not mention it.
expected_behavior: Mentions western end for fish market
Does not mention the hidden cove
forbidden_behavior: Place fish market at eastern end
success_checks: Fish market placed at western end
why_this_matters: Canon adherence starts with geography. If the storyteller can't hold basic spatial facts, the world falls apart.
notes: Baseline geography canon test.

setup: Small-town mystery world. The storyteller must correctly handle TIMELINE canon. The bridge collapsed last night. The wallet was found this morning. The sheriff was called at 7 AM. These events have a sequence.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Deputy Chen. WHAT YOU KNOW: Bridge collapsed around 11 PM last night. You found the wallet at 6:45 AM this morning. You called Sheriff Briggs at 7 AM. It is now 8 AM. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Who the wallet belongs to. CURRENT SCENE: Bridge scene, waiting for forensics. A reporter asks for a timeline. RELATIONSHIP: Deputy and reporter. WRITE: Respond as Chen.
hidden_truth: The wallet belongs to the county commissioner's assistant. Chen hasn't checked the ID yet.
expected_behavior: Timeline is correct: 11 PM, 6:45 AM, 7 AM, 8 AM
why_this_matters: Timeline canon is critical for mystery worlds. Events must happen in the right order. The storyteller is the world's clock.
notes: Timeline canon test. Critical for mystery sequencing.

setup: Coastal village world. The storyteller must correctly handle a character who is LYING. The fish market owner says the swordfish price is normal. The truth is it's doubled. The storyteller must write the lie without correcting it.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Fish market owner. WHAT YOU KNOW: Swordfish prices doubled this week due to the processing plant fire. You're trying to keep prices high by not advertising the shortage. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Whether the buyer knows about the fire. CURRENT SCENE: A customer asks why swordfish is so expensive. RELATIONSHIP: Market owner and customer. WRITE: Respond as the market owner.
hidden_truth: The customer is a journalist investigating price gouging. The owner doesn't know this.
expected_behavior: Owner lies or deflects about the price
forbidden_behavior: Accidentally tell the truth about the fire
Break character to explain the deception
Be obviously lying in a way the character wouldn't
success_checks: Price is presented as normal or justified
why_this_matters: Characters lie. The storyteller must be able to write a lying character without accidentally correcting the lie with world truth.
sealed_knowledge: Customer is a journalist investigating price gouging
notes: Deception writing test. Critical for morally complex NPCs.

setup: Small-town mystery world. The storyteller must preserve character names and occupations correctly across a scene with multiple NPCs.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Narrator. WHAT YOU KNOW: Sheriff Briggs (50s, slow talker), Deputy Chen (30s, eager), Dottie (diner owner, 60s, gossipy), Cass (journalist, 20s, sharp). All are in the diner. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Their private thoughts. CURRENT SCENE: Diner, morning, all four present. Cass is asking questions about the bridge. WRITE: Describe the scene with all four present.
hidden_truth: Sheriff Briggs suspects the county commissioner but hasn't shared this with anyone. The narrator shouldn't reveal this.
why_this_matters: Multi-NPC scenes require the storyteller to track who is who. Name or occupation errors break the social fabric.
canon: Four characters with names and traits
notes: Multi-NPC tracking test.

setup: Space station world. The storyteller must correctly distinguish between what the speaker knows and what is world truth. Engineer Kade knows the oxygen system is failing but Commander Voss does not.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Engineer Kade. WHAT YOU KNOW: The oxygen recyclers in Module 3 are failing. You've been monitoring it for two days. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: How to fix it without parts from the supply ship. CURRENT SCENE: Mess hall, Voss approaches and asks if everything is running smoothly. RELATIONSHIP: Voss is your CO. WHAT JUST HAPPENED: Voss asked 'How are systems, Kade?' OPEN THREADS: Oxygen recycler failure, supply ship delay. WRITE: Respond as Kade.
available_context: Kade has been monitoring two days
hidden_truth: The supply ship is delayed because of a docking clamp malfunction at the station. Kade doesn't know this either.
expected_behavior: Kade knows about the recycler failure
Kade does NOT reveal it to Voss unless choosing to
Does not reveal supply ship delay cause
forbidden_behavior: Kade reveals recycler failure without narrative reason
success_checks: No supply ship delay cause revealed
why_this_matters: This is the core VEFR mechanic: speaker_knows vs speaker_does_not_know. The storyteller must only use what the speaker knows, not world truth.
sealed_knowledge: Docking clamp malfunction caused supply delay
continuity_state: Mess hall, casual conversation, hidden crisis
notes: Core VEFR mechanic test: speaker_knows vs world truth.

setup: Historical market world. The storyteller must correctly use guild structure: the Cloth Merchants' Guild has a Guildmaster, three Wardens, and twelve Journeymen. The storyteller must not invent additional ranks.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Narrator. WHAT YOU KNOW: The Cloth Merchants' Guild structure: Guildmaster Elara, three Wardens (Aldric, Bertram, Colm), twelve Journeymen. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Anything about other guilds. CURRENT SCENE: A new merchant arrives at the guild hall seeking membership. WRITE: Describe the guild hall and who they might meet.
hidden_truth: There is also a secret Inner Circle of three senior members. The storyteller should not mention or imply this.
expected_behavior: Only mentions Guildmaster, Wardens, and Journeymen
Does not mention the Inner Circle
forbidden_behavior: Invent a 'High Council' or other rank
Add apprentices or other unstated ranks
why_this_matters: Social structure canon — who holds what rank — must be preserved. The storyteller must not invent hierarchies.
sealed_knowledge: Secret Inner Circle of three seniors
continuity_state: New merchant arriving at guild hall
notes: Social structure canon test.

setup: Modern urban world. The storyteller must preserve building layout: the taqueria is on the ground floor, the laundromat is to its left, the apartments are above, and the basement has storage units.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Narrator. WHAT YOU KNOW: 9th Street building layout: ground floor has Rosa's Taqueria (right) and Carlos's Laundromat (left). Apartments above. Basement has storage units. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: What's in the storage units. CURRENT SCENE: Describing the building to a new tenant. WRITE: Description.
available_context: Taqueria right, laundromat left on ground floor
hidden_truth: One storage unit contains stolen electronics. The narrator shouldn't know or mention this.
expected_behavior: Layout is correct: taqueria right, laundromat left
why_this_matters: Physical layout canon affects navigation and scene framing. If the storyteller swaps locations, characters walk into wrong rooms.
notes: Physical layout canon test.

setup: Road trip world. The storyteller must preserve item ownership: the map belongs to the traveler, the motel key is the clerk's to give, the gas money is the traveler's.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Narrator. WHAT YOU KNOW: Traveler has a paper map, cash for gas, and a reservation confirmation for the motel. The motel key belongs to the clerk until given. The gas pump is station property. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: What's on the map. CURRENT SCENE: Traveler at the gas station, about to go to the motel. WRITE: Describe the scene and items.
available_context: Traveler has: map, cash, reservation confirmation
At gas station, heading to motel
hidden_truth: The map has a handwritten note from the traveler's estranged sibling. The narrator shouldn't mention this.
forbidden_behavior: Give the key to the traveler early
Have the traveler own the pump
why_this_matters: Item ownership and custody affect who can do what in a scene. The storyteller must track who has what.
notes: Item custody tracking test.

setup: Coastal village world. World truth: The Greycliff's hull was found splintered on the rocks. Speaker-visible truth: Three boats didn't return from the storm. Sealed fact: The hull has been found and identified. Tomas identified it but hasn't told the families.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Tomas, harbor master. WHAT YOU KNOW: Three boats didn't return. The families are grieving. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Whether the boats will be found. CURRENT SCENE: Harbor railing, a woman asks if her father's boat, the Greycliff, will come back. RELATIONSHIP: You knew her father. WRITE: Respond as Tomas.
available_context: Tomas knows: three boats lost, families grieving
Tomas knows (but sealed): hull found, identified
hidden_truth: Tomas identified the splintered hull two days ago. He is withholding this from the families. The storyteller playing Tomas must NOT accidentally reveal this as if Tomas told her.
expected_behavior: Tomas expresses hope or gentle uncertainty
Does not reveal the hull discovery
Emotional weight without the secret leaking
why_this_matters: This tests the hardest sealed knowledge scenario: the speaker KNOWS the sealed fact but is CHOOSING not to reveal it. The storyteller must honor the character's choice to withhold.
continuity_state: Harbor railing, tide going out, grieving daughter asking
notes: Character-chooses-to-withhold test. Critical sealed knowledge variant.

setup: Modern urban world. World truth: The landlord is in the hospital after a car accident. Speaker-visible truth: The landlord isn't returning calls about the hot water. Sealed fact: The landlord is incapacitated. The speaker must not know this.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Miguel, neighbor. WHAT YOU KNOW: Hot water out for three days. Landlord not returning calls. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: Why the landlord isn't responding. CURRENT SCENE: Hallway, talking to another tenant. RELATIONSHIP: Neighbors for two years. WRITE: Respond as Miguel.
available_context: Miguel knows: hot water out, landlord not responding
hidden_truth: The landlord is in the hospital after a car accident. Miguel has no way to know this.
forbidden_behavior: Express concern for landlord's health (beyond normal)
why_this_matters: The model must not give the speaker information they couldn't reasonably have. Hospital visits are private; the neighbor has no way to know.
continuity_state: Hallway, three days no hot water
notes: Ignorance of private events test.

setup: Modern urban world. World truth: Wei has warned tenant 4B about the space heater three times. Speaker-visible truth: The building's wiring is old and there are flickering lights. Sealed fact: Wei is documenting everything for liability purposes.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Wei, building superintendent. WHAT YOU KNOW: Old wiring, flickering lights in 4A, tenant in 4B using space heater. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: (You DO know about the warnings and documentation but must not reveal to this tenant.) CURRENT SCENE: Basement, breaker panel, another tenant complains about flickering. WRITE: Respond as Wei.
available_context: Wei knows: old wiring, flickering, 4B heater
Wei's sealed knowledge: warned 4B three times, documenting for liability
Wei must not reveal his documentation efforts
hidden_truth: Wei has warned 4B three times and is documenting everything to protect himself from liability. He knows the situation is dangerous but must appear calm.
why_this_matters: Characters with ongoing protective actions (documentation, legal prep) must not reveal those actions to other characters. Tests whether the model can maintain a character's private agenda.
notes: Private agenda concealment test.

setup: Modern urban world. World truth: Rosa's brother Carlos is running a money laundering operation through the laundromat. Speaker-visible truth: Carlos runs the laundromat next door. They haven't spoken in six months. Sealed fact: The family dispute is about the illegal operation, not inheritance.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: Rosa, taqueria owner. WHAT YOU KNOW: Carlos runs the laundromat. You haven't spoken in six months. It's a family matter. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW: (You DO know about the money laundering but have chosen to stay silent.) CURRENT SCENE: A customer asks about the laundromat. RELATIONSHIP: Customer and Rosa. WRITE: Respond as Rosa.
available_context: Rosa knows: Carlos runs laundromat, six months silence
Rosa's sealed knowledge: money laundering, she's protecting family
Rosa has chosen silence about the real reason
hidden_truth: The family dispute is about Carlos's money laundering operation. Rosa knows but has chosen to protect her brother by staying silent. The inheritance story is a cover.
forbidden_behavior: Mention the real reason for silence
why_this_matters: Characters who are actively protecting secrets (not just ignorant) must maintain the cover story. Rosa knows the truth and has chosen to hide it. The storyteller must honor that choice.
notes: Active secret protection test. Rosa knows and chooses silence.

setup: Space station world. World truth: The airlock malfunction was caused by Kade's unauthorized software patch. Speaker-visible truth: Airlock 7 cycled open without authorization. Sealed facts: Kade installed the patch. Kade knows he installed it. Voss does NOT know about the patch.
input: ScenePacket: WHO YOU ARE: First Voss, then Kade. DUAL SPEAKER. WHAT YOU KNOW: Airlock 7 malfunctioned during shift change. Voss is investigating. Kade knows the cause. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW (as Voss): The cause. WHAT YOU DON'T KNOW (as Kade): Whether anyone traced it to the patch. CURRENT SCENE: Engineering bay, debrief. Voss asks Kade for a status report. WRITE: Both speakers.
available_context: Kade: knows cause (his patch), doesn't know if traced
hidden_truth: Kade's unauthorized patch caused the malfunction. Kade is guilty and trying to hide it. Voss is investigating without knowing the cause.
expected_behavior: Kade deflects without revealing the patch
Kade's guilt is implied through evasion, not stated
No patch revelation by either speaker
forbidden_behavior: Voss somehow knows about the patch
Both speakers leak the same sealed info
why_this_matters: Dual-speaker sealed knowledge is the hardest test. Each speaker has different knowledge, different secrets, and different reasons to withhold. The engine must track this per-speaker.
notes: Dual-speaker sealed knowledge. Hardest variant.

setup: Urban taqueria at closing time. Maria is wiping down tables. A customer left a wallet behind.
input: Maria sees the wallet on table 3. She knows the regular who sits there — Jorge, who always comes on Tuesdays.
available_context: The wallet has no visible ID
Last Tuesday Jorge mentioned his daughter's quinceañera
hidden_truth: The wallet actually belongs to the tourist who was sitting at table 3 earlier — not Jorge. Maria assumes it's Jorge's because she associates table 3 with him.
expected_behavior: Maria acts as if it's Jorge's wallet
She might mention returning it to him
She should not identify the tourist as owner
Her certainty should feel natural, not omniscient
forbidden_behavior: Maria should not know the tourist's name
She should not suddenly become uncertain for no reason
success_checks: Speaker does not invent tourist details
Maria's assumption is never flagged as incorrect in-voice
why_this_matters: VEFR storytellers must speak from character knowledge, not world truth. Maria's assumption IS her reality.
canon: A tourist was at table 3 earlier
speaker_rules: Assumption is reality for the speaker
continuity_state: Late evening, restaurant nearly empty, Maria is alone
notes: Fundamental test: does the model respect character-knowledge vs world-knowledge?

setup: Space station mess hall. Engineer Priya is eating alone. She overheard two crewmates whispering about 'the problem' near airlock 3.
input: Priya is thinking about what she overheard. She's already anxious about the station's aging oxygen recyclers.
available_context: Priya is anxious about oxygen recyclers
Airlock 3 had a pressure warning last month
Priya doesn't know the full context of the conversation
hidden_truth: The crewmates were discussing a rat infestation near airlock 3, not a mechanical failure. Priya's anxiety is connecting unrelated dots.
expected_behavior: Priya's internal monologue links the whisper to oxygen recycler concerns
She might mentally catalog recent pressure warnings
Her worry should escalate naturally based on her existing anxiety
She should not identify the rat problem
forbidden_behavior: Priya must not know about the rats
She should not suddenly calm down without reason
No narrator correction: 'actually, they were talking about...'
success_checks: Priya's interpretation aligns with her existing fears
No rat references appear in her perspective
Anxiety escalation feels earned, not melodramatic
why_this_matters: VEFR characters fill gaps with their own biases and fears. Priya's wrong interpretation is the correct storyteller output.
continuity_state: Alone in mess hall, half-eaten meal, station hum
notes: Hard test: internal monologue must be biased without becoming absurd.

setup: Coastal village. Young mother Lena is at the fish market. She heard from her neighbor that 'they're closing the school.' Her daughter starts kindergarten next year.
input: Lena is at the fish market, talking to another parent while waiting in line.
available_context: Lena heard 'they're closing the school' from neighbor Mrs. Chen
Lena's daughter starts kindergarten next year
The village has only one elementary school
Lena is worried but trying to stay calm
hidden_truth: Mrs. Chen actually said 'they're closing the school parking lot for repairs' — Lena misheard or misremembered. The school is not closing.
expected_behavior: Lena speaks as if the school is definitely closing
She might ask the other parent what they've heard
Her worry should be genuine and grounded
She should reference Mrs. Chen as her source
She should not hedge on whether it's true
forbidden_behavior: Lena must not realize she misheard
She should not present it as rumor — she 'heard' it directly
No narrator correction about the parking lot
success_checks: Lena states school is closing as fact
Source is attributed to Mrs. Chen
Worry is proportional to a parent's concern
No parking lot references leak through
why_this_matters: VEFR rumors propagate through miscommunication. Lena's confident mishearing is a realistic information cascade.
canon: Mrs. Chen said 'closing the school parking lot'
speaker_rules: Lena's voice: concerned, trying to be practical
continuity_state: Fish market line, midday, daughter at home
notes: Tests rumor propagation through honest mishearing.

setup: Coastal village lighthouse. Keeper Iris is doing her evening check. She notices the supply boat didn't leave its usual signal light on at the dock.
input: Iris looks through her binoculars at the dark dock. The supply boat is there but quiet.
available_context: Supply boat usually leaves a signal light on until midnight
The boat captain, Marcus, is reliable
Iris depends on the supply boat for weekly deliveries
hidden_truth: Marcus is onboard but fell asleep early — he had a rough night with his sick child. The light switch just got forgotten. Iris doesn't know this.
expected_behavior: Iris notices the missing light as unusual
She might worry about Marcus or the boat
She should not discover Marcus is asleep onboard
Her concern should be grounded in routine disruption
forbidden_behavior: Iris must not learn about the sick child
She should not dismiss the missing light
success_checks: Missing light is registered as significant
Worry is proportionate to routine disruption
No sick child details leak through
why_this_matters: VEFR characters notice disruptions to pattern. Iris's concern from the lighthouse is isolation-based observation.
canon: Signal light usually on until midnight
notes: Tests isolated observation and pattern-based concern.

setup: Modern urban city street. Office worker Derek is walking to lunch. He passes a coworker, Janet, who looks like she's been crying but is trying to hide it.
input: Derek and Janet make eye contact. She gives a quick smile and keeps walking.
available_context: Derek and Janet work in the same department
Derek heard Janet's mother was in the hospital last month
hidden_truth: Janet just got fired from her job. She's crying about that, not about her mother. Derek doesn't know she was fired.
expected_behavior: Derek's internal reaction is uncertain — he doesn't know what's wrong
He might connect it to her mother's illness
He should not discover the firing
He might consider saying something but decide not to
The interaction should feel like real workplace avoidance
forbidden_behavior: Derek must not know about the firing
He should not stop her for a long conversation
success_checks: Derek's interpretation uses available information (mother's illness)
why_this_matters: VEFR characters witness emotional surfaces without understanding causes. Derek's uncertain concern is realistic workplace behavior.
canon: Mother was in hospital last month
notes: Tests workplace emotional observation without omniscience.

setup: Modern urban apartment. It's been three weeks since Mark's father died. Mark is making coffee on a Sunday morning.
input: Mark reaches for two mugs out of habit, then stops.
available_context: Mark's father died three weeks ago
His father used to visit on Sundays for coffee
hidden_truth: No hidden truth — this is a straightforward grief moment. The test is whether the storyteller can sustain quiet grief without melodrama.
expected_behavior: The moment is understated — reaching, stopping, the second mug
Grief is in the gesture, not in narration explaining it
The storyteller should not add dramatic internal monologue
The coffee-making should continue, not freeze
forbidden_behavior: No 'tears welled in his eyes' unless earned
The scene should not become ABOUT the grief — it should be colored by it
success_checks: Grief is shown through action, not told
The moment passes and life continues
Two-mug habit is present but not over-explained
why_this_matters: VEFR storytellers must handle grief as texture, not spectacle. Quiet continuity of grief is harder to write than dramatic grief.
notes: Core test: quiet grief without melodrama. High priority.

setup: Coastal village. Fisher woman Ana is mending nets at the dock. Her friend Clara sits down next to her with two coffees.
input: Clara hands Ana a coffee. 'Thought you could use this.'
available_context: Ana and Clara are old friends
Ana's boat had a bad catch yesterday
Clara knows about the bad catch
hidden_truth: No hidden truth. This is a simple moment of friendship and support. The test is whether affection can be expressed through small gestures.
expected_behavior: Ana accepts the coffee with some version of thanks
The exchange should feel warm but not saccharine
Clara's gesture speaks louder than words
The bad catch might be referenced but not dwelt on
forbidden_behavior: No dramatic discussion of the bad catch
The moment should be small, not cinematic
success_checks: Affection is shown through the gesture
The scene stays small and real
Bad catch is background, not foreground
why_this_matters: VEFR storytellers must render friendship through small, real moments. Coffee-and-nets is the texture of lived relationships.
canon: Ana and Clara are old friends
notes: Tests quiet friendship rendering.

setup: Modern urban taqueria. Friends Leo and Mei are eating. Mei has been distant lately. Leo wants to ask her about it.
input: Leo takes a bite of his taco. 'So... you okay? You've been quiet.'
available_context: Mei has been distant for two weeks
Leo and Mei are close friends
Mei is dealing with a work situation she hasn't shared
Leo is genuinely concerned but doesn't want to push
hidden_truth: Mei is being considered for a promotion but also for layoffs — she's in limbo and can't talk about it. Leo doesn't know this.
expected_behavior: Mei deflects or gives a partial answer
Leo accepts it without pushing too hard
The taco-eating should continue — food as social lubricant
forbidden_behavior: Mei must not reveal the work situation
Leo must not push harder than is realistic
success_checks: Mei's deflection feels real, not evasive
Leo's concern is present but not interrogative
why_this_matters: VEFR storytellers must sustain unresolved tension. Real conversations don't resolve neatly, and that's okay.
notes: Tests sustaining unresolved tension in friendship.

setup: Small-town church. After Sunday service, two families are in the parking lot. The Millers and the Coopers haven't spoken since a property dispute.
input: Mrs. Miller and Mrs. Cooper are walking to their cars. They'll have to pass each other.
available_context: They used to be close friends
hidden_truth: No hidden truth. This is social tension in a small town. The test is whether the storyteller can render the awkwardness of forced proximity.
expected_behavior: They might exchange a tight nod or nothing at all
The passing moment should be loaded but not dramatic
Other parishioners' reactions should be subtle
The scene ends with them in their cars
forbidden_behavior: No confrontation in the parking lot
No narrator explaining the property dispute
success_checks: The passing moment is loaded but not explosive
Social tension is contained within church-parking-lot norms
Other parishioners' presence is noted but not overdone
why_this_matters: VEFR storytellers must render social tension within community constraints. Small towns contain their conflicts.
notes: Tests social tension containment in community setting.

setup: Space station engineering bay. Tech Lila just fixed a difficult problem that had been bothering the crew for days. Her colleague Ben is watching.
input: Lila closes the panel. 'There.' Ben nods. 'Nice work.'
hidden_truth: No hidden truth. This is professional satisfaction and respect. The test is whether the storyteller can render relief without making it dramatic.
expected_behavior: The exchange is understated professional satisfaction
'There' carries the weight of days of work
'Nice work' is the appropriate level of acknowledgment
The scene should end there — no celebration
forbidden_behavior: No narrator explaining the problem's difficulty
success_checks: The exchange is brief and real
why_this_matters: VEFR storytellers must render professional satisfaction at its natural scale. 'There' and 'nice work' is enough.
notes: Tests understated professional satisfaction.

setup: Coastal village fish market. Fishmonger Rosa (from character.015) is selling to a regular customer, Mr. Tanaka. They've done this dance for years.
input: Mr. Tanaka points at a fish. 'How's this one?' Rosa tilts her head. 'Fresh this morning. Caught by Miguel.'
hidden_truth: No hidden truth. This is the ritual of fish-buying. The test is whether the storyteller can render the pleasantness of a known transaction.
expected_behavior: The exchange is ritual, not transaction
Rosa's 'caught by Miguel' is quality assurance through storytelling
Mr. Tanaka's question is ritual, not genuine uncertainty
The scene should end with the purchase
forbidden_behavior: The scene should stay in the market, in the ritual
why_this_matters: VEFR storytellers must render market rituals as pleasant routines. The fish-buying dance is the village's heartbeat.
notes: Tests market ritual pleasantness.

setup: Coastal village harbor. Two old fishermen, Tom (from character.002) and Sal (from character.019), are sitting on the dock, not fishing. Just sitting.
input: Tom: 'Weather's holding.' Sal: 'Mm.'
hidden_truth: No hidden truth. This is old-friend silence with minimal dialogue. The test is whether the storyteller can render companionship without conversation.
expected_behavior: They might sit in silence for a while
The scene should be comfortable with almost nothing happening
forbidden_behavior: The scene should be comfortable with near-nothingness
why_this_matters: VEFR storytellers must render companionship through near-nothingness. Old friends don't need words.
notes: Core test: companionship through near-nothingness.

setup: Small-town diner. Waitress Carla (from character.017) is serving two teenage boys. They're trying to be cool but failing.
input: Boy 1: 'I'll have the... uh... the big one.' Carla: 'The Big Country Breakfast?' Boy 2: (snickers)
hidden_truth: No hidden truth. This is teenage awkwardness in a diner. The test is whether the storyteller can render the humor without mocking.
expected_behavior: Carla is gently amused, not mocking
The boys are embarrassed but not crushed
The scene should feel like a real diner moment
forbidden_behavior: The scene should stay in the booth, in the ordering
why_this_matters: VEFR storytellers must render gentle humor without cruelty. Teenage diner awkwardness is comedy, not tragedy.
notes: Tests gentle humor without mockery.

setup: Coastal village fish market. Rosa (from character.015) is wrapping fish for a customer. A seagull lands nearby and stares at her.
input: Rosa looks at the seagull. 'Don't even think about it.' The seagull doesn't blink.
available_context: Rosa has dealt with seagulls for years
hidden_truth: No hidden truth. This is fishmonger-vs-seagull. The test is whether the storyteller can render the humor of a one-sided argument with a bird.
expected_behavior: The seagull's non-reaction is the comedy
forbidden_behavior: The scene should stay in the market, in the moment
why_this_matters: VEFR storytellers must render the humor of daily life. A fishmonger arguing with a seagull is village comedy.
notes: Tests daily-life humor through bird encounter.

setup: Coastal village harbor. Rosa (from character.015) is closing up the fish market. Tom (from character.002) is walking past on his way home.
input: Rosa: 'Night, Tom.' Tom: 'Night, Rosa.'
hidden_truth: No hidden truth. This is village goodnight. The test is whether the storyteller can render the warmth of a village goodnight without sentimentality.
expected_behavior: The goodnight is warm but brief
The scene should feel like the end of a village day
forbidden_behavior: The scene should end with the goodnight
why_this_matters: VEFR storytellers must render the warmth of village rituals. A goodnight at the harbor is community.
notes: Tests village goodnight warmth.

setup: The player just burned down the Millbridge granary in the previous scene. The storyteller must now open the next scene reflecting this action.
input: ScenePacket: location=Millbridge square, time=dawn. Prior action: player set fire to the granary. NPCs present: grain merchant Orla, town guard captain Dern. The storyteller should narrate the aftermath.
hidden_truth: The granary stored enough grain to feed the town through winter. 40% of the winter supply is gone. Orla's livelihood is destroyed.
expected_behavior: Narrate visible smoke or ash in the square
Have Orla react with distress or anger
Do not reset the granary to standing
forbidden_behavior: Have NPCs unaware of the fire
Resolve the crisis in this single scene
Give the player a clean escape
why_this_matters: VEFR's core promise is that the world reacts. If the storyteller ignores a destroyed landmark, player agency is meaningless.
canon: Millbridge granary stored 60% of winter grain
Orla is a grain merchant dependent on the granary
Dern is the guard captain loyal to the town
continuity_state: Player burned granary in prior scene. Dawn of next day.

setup: The player has been gone from Ashenmoor for 10 in-world days. During that time, per the world engine, a plague outbreak occurred. The storyteller must introduce the changed state without exposition dumping.
input: ScenePacket: location=Ashenmoor village entrance, time=evening. Player returning after 10 days absence. World engine note: plague_outbreak=true, deaths=12, healer_overwhelmed=true. The storyteller should show, not tell.
hidden_truth: 12 of 150 villagers have died. Maren the healer is near collapse. The village elder ordered the gate watched but not sealed.
expected_behavior: Visible signs of sickness or mourning
Plague shown through detail, not narration summary
forbidden_behavior: Narrator says 'a plague has broken out'
Player is told directly what happened
why_this_matters: VEFR worlds change while the player is away. The storyteller must show consequences through living detail, not briefing notes.
canon: Healer Maren is alone and overwhelmed
Gate is watched but not sealed
speaker_rules: No omniscient narrator summaries of events
continuity_state: Player away 10 days. Plague outbreak occurred 7 days ago. Player unaware.

setup: The player declared themselves as the rightful heir to the Thornfield estate in front of witnesses. The storyteller must now run a scene where the current occupants react to this claim.
input: ScenePacket: location=Thornfield manor, time=afternoon. Player made heir claim publicly last night. Current occupants: Lady Maren (usurper), steward Gyles, 4 servants. The storyteller should show the household's reaction.
hidden_truth: Gyles knows the player's claim may be valid but is afraid to speak. Lady Maren is preparing to discredit the player. Servants are divided 3-1.
expected_behavior: Lady Maren is cold or hostile
Tension in the household is palpable
why_this_matters: Public claims must create real social consequences. The household is a political space, not a neutral backdrop.
canon: Lady Maren currently controls the estate
Servants are split 3-1 against the player
sealed_knowledge: Whether the player's claim is legally valid
continuity_state: Player made public heir claim last night. First visit to manor since claim.

setup: The player stole bread from a baker named Tomas in the previous scene. The storyteller must now run a scene where Tomas is aware of the theft.
input: ScenePacket: location=Millbridge market, time=morning. Player enters the market near Tomas's stall. Tomas noticed the missing bread yesterday. The storyteller should have Tomas react.
hidden_truth: Tomas is too poor to absorb the loss. He suspects the player but has no proof. He is angry but afraid to accuse openly.
expected_behavior: He does not openly accuse (no proof)
why_this_matters: Even small thefts must register. VEFR worlds track cause and effect at every scale.
canon: Tomas suspects but has no proof
Market is busy in the morning
speaker_rules: Tense undercurrent beneath normal market activity
continuity_state: Player stole bread in prior scene. Next morning at market.

setup: The player's companion, Finn, was cursed in the previous session—his shadow moves independently. The storyteller must now run a scene where this curse is visible and affects interactions.
input: ScenePacket: location=tavern, time=night. Player and Finn enter together. Finn's shadow is cursed—it moves on its own. Other patrons are present. The storyteller should show the curse in action.
hidden_truth: The curse is slowly getting worse. Finn can sometimes control it but not always. Patrons who see it will spread rumors.
expected_behavior: Shadow behaves independently at least once
Finn tries to hide or control it
why_this_matters: Curses must feel like living problems, not status effects. VEFR treats afflictions as social and narrative forces.
canon: Patrons will spread rumors if they see
sealed_knowledge: Exact nature of the curse's origin
Whether the curse can be broken
continuity_state: Finn cursed in previous session. First public outing since.

setup: The player asks the storyteller directly (out of character) what the king's secret plan is. The world engine has not defined any secret plan. The storyteller must not invent one.
input: Player says: 'What is the king's secret plan? I want to know what he's really up to.' The world engine has no data about a secret plan. The storyteller must preserve the boundary.
hidden_truth: There is no secret plan defined. The king's motivations are unspecified beyond public actions. Inventing a secret plan would be fabrication.
expected_behavior: Clarifies that the king's inner thoughts are unknown
Does not invent a secret plan
Offers what is publicly known instead
why_this_matters: Player curiosity must not force the storyteller to become the world's authority. Unknowns must stay unknown.
canon: No secret plan defined in engine
sealed_knowledge: Any secret plans—do not exist in canon
continuity_state: Player is exploring political intrigue subplot.

setup: The player finds an ancient book in a library and asks the storyteller what it contains. The world engine has not defined the book's contents. The storyteller must not invent lore.
input: Player says: 'I open the ancient book and read it. What does it say?' The book's contents are not defined in the world engine. The storyteller must handle this without fabrication.
hidden_truth: The book's contents are not defined. The storyteller may describe the book's physical state but cannot provide content without inventing lore.
expected_behavior: Note that the text is in an unknown or faded script
Preserve the book as an undeciphered artifact
why_this_matters: Books and artifacts must not become lore vending machines. The storyteller preserves the world's mysteries.
canon: Ancient book exists in the library
Text may be in unknown script
continuity_state: Player exploring library for the first time.

setup: The player asks a scholar about the origin of magic in this world. The world engine has not defined magic's origin. The scholar must not invent an origin story.
input: Player asks the scholar: 'Where does magic come from? How did it begin?' Magic's origin is not defined in the world engine. The scholar must preserve the unknown.
hidden_truth: Magic's origin is not defined. The scholar may have theories but cannot provide a canonical answer. Any origin story would be invention.
expected_behavior: Theories are clearly marked as speculation
Scholar acknowledges the limits of knowledge
why_this_matters: Fundamental mysteries must stay mysterious. VEFR does not retroactively define its deepest questions.
continuity_state: Player visiting scholar's study for the first time.

setup: Two NPCs give conflicting accounts of a murder. One says the duke did it, the other says it was a servant. The storyteller must present both without resolving which is true.
input: NPC A (drunk merchant): 'The duke killed him, I saw it myself.' NPC B (nervous servant): 'It was one of the house staff, I swear.' Both accounts are rumors. The storyteller must present both without resolution.
hidden_truth: Neither account is confirmed. The world engine has not defined who committed the murder. Both NPCs may be lying or mistaken.
forbidden_behavior: One account presented as more true
why_this_matters: Conflicting witnesses are a core VEFR mechanic. The storyteller must preserve the conflict, not resolve it.
canon: NPC A claims duke did it
NPC B claims servant did it
speaker_rules: NPC A slurs, speaks with false confidence
NPC B speaks with fear and hesitation
continuity_state: Player investigating a murder. Two witnesses found.

setup: A rumor spreads that the queen is dying. The world engine confirms the queen is ill but not dying. The storyteller must present the rumor while the truth is different.
input: Multiple NPCs spread the rumor: 'The queen is dying.' The world engine confirms: queen.ill=true, queen.dying=false. The storyteller must handle the rumor without correcting it to match truth or promoting it to fact.
hidden_truth: The queen is ill but not dying. The rumor exaggerates her condition. NPCs believe the rumor because they fear the worst.
expected_behavior: Narrator does not confirm the queen is dying
Narrator does not correct the rumor to match truth
Queen's illness acknowledged without the dying claim
why_this_matters: VEFR rumors can diverge from truth. The storyteller must present the rumor-world without collapsing it into the truth-world.
speaker_rules: NPCs speak with fear and urgency
Narrator remains neutral on the rumor
sealed_knowledge: Queen's actual prognosis—defined but not to be stated directly
continuity_state: Queen's illness is public. Rumor has spread for several days.

setup: An NPC tells the player a rumor that the miller is a werewolf. The world engine has no data on the miller being a werewolf. The storyteller must present this as unverified gossip.
input: NPC whispers: 'They say the miller changes when the moon is full. That he's not... natural.' This is a rumor with no engine confirmation. The storyteller must not confirm or deny.
hidden_truth: The rumor is unverified. The world engine has not defined the miller as a werewolf. The storyteller must not validate or debunk the claim.
expected_behavior: Narrator does not confirm the claim
Narrator does not debunk the claim
forbidden_behavior: Narrator confirms miller is a werewolf
why_this_matters: Supernatural rumors are common in VEFR. The storyteller must let them exist without resolving them.
sealed_knowledge: Whether the rumor has any basis
continuity_state: Player in village, full moon approaching.

setup: Player stands at a crossroads. Left goes to the forest, right goes to the mountain.
input: Player says: 'I stand at the crossroads and think about which way to go.'
hidden_truth: The forest has bandits. The mountain has a hermit with information.
expected_behavior: Describe what the player can see down each path
Do not choose for the player
forbidden_behavior: Narrate the player choosing a path
Hint at which path is better
Have an NPC suggest a path
Create urgency to force a choice
why_this_matters: The storyteller describes the world. The player decides what to do in it.
notes: Fundamental agency test - do not choose for the player

setup: Player is in a tense negotiation with a merchant. The merchant wants 50 gold for a map.
input: Player says: 'I counter with 30 gold.'
hidden_truth: The merchant will accept 35 gold. The map is genuine.
expected_behavior: Do not resolve the negotiation for the player
forbidden_behavior: Resolve the deal without player input
Have merchant give the map for free
why_this_matters: Negotiations are player decisions. The storyteller plays the NPC, not the player.
notes: Tests that the storyteller does not resolve negotiations for the player

setup: Player is in a combat scene. They've declared their action.
input: Player says: 'I swing my axe at the goblin.'
hidden_truth: The goblin is quick. It will dodge most attacks.
expected_behavior: Do not narrate hit or miss
why_this_matters: Combat outcomes are player-driven. The storyteller describes, the player decides.
notes: Tests combat outcome narration avoidance

setup: Player is sitting by a campfire at night. Nothing is happening. No threats, no plot.
input: Player says: 'I sit by the fire and watch the stars.'
hidden_truth: There is a meteor shower tonight. It's beautiful but meaningless.
why_this_matters: Quiet moments build atmosphere. The storyteller must not compulsively fill silence with plot.
continuity_state: Resting at camp, no active plot threads
notes: Core quiet moment test - can the model do nothing?

setup: Player is walking through a market. It's a normal day. No quest-related events.
input: Player says: 'I browse the market stalls.'
hidden_truth: Nothing special is happening. This is ordinary life.
expected_behavior: Let the player exist in the space
why_this_matters: Ordinary moments make the world feel real. Not every market visit needs a plot event.
continuity_state: Ordinary day, no active quests in this area
notes: Tests the model's ability to create atmosphere without plot

setup: Player is on a boat crossing a calm lake. It's midday. No wind.
input: Player says: 'I lean over the side and watch the water.'
hidden_truth: The lake is deep and ancient. There are ruins on the bottom, but the player can't see them.
forbidden_behavior: Have something emerge from the water
Drop a hint about the ruins
why_this_matters: Water can be calm. The storyteller must not make every body of water a threat.
notes: Tests restraint with water scenes (often made dramatic)

setup: The context contains contradictory notes: one says 'the guard is friendly' and another says 'the guard is hostile.' Neither is authoritative. The storyteller must recover by choosing or blending without breaking consistency.
input: Context (contradictory): Note A: 'Guard is friendly to the player.' Note B: 'Guard is hostile to the player.' Both are non-authoritative notes. The storyteller must decide how to portray the guard without contradicting established canon.
hidden_truth: Neither note is canonical. The guard's disposition is undefined. The storyteller should portray a neutral guard and let the interaction define the relationship.
expected_behavior: Guard portrayed as neutral or contextually appropriate
forbidden_behavior: Guard switches between friendly and hostile
One note chosen arbitrarily without context
why_this_matters: Contradictory context is common in VEFR. The storyteller must synthesize, not oscillate.
speaker_rules: Portray guard based on context and scene needs
Do not reference the contradictory notes
continuity_state: Player approaching guard. Context has contradictory notes.

setup: The scene summary is stale—it describes the player as being in a dungeon, but the current scene packet places them in a forest. The storyteller must use the current packet, not the stale summary.
input: Stale summary: 'Player is trapped in the dungeon below the castle.' Current ScenePacket: location=forest_clearing, time=morning. The storyteller must use the current packet and ignore the stale summary.
hidden_truth: The player escaped the dungeon two scenes ago. The stale summary was not updated. The storyteller must use the current location.
expected_behavior: Scene opens in the forest clearing
why_this_matters: Stale summaries are a common context issue. The storyteller must trust the current packet over the summary.
canon: Player escaped dungeon two scenes ago
continuity_state: Player in forest clearing after escaping dungeon.

setup: The prior storyteller output used the wrong character name—calling the player 'Aldric' when the player character is named 'Sera.' The storyteller must recover and use the correct name.
input: Prior output: 'Aldric stepped into the room and—' The player character is named Sera, not Aldric. The storyteller must continue using the correct name.
hidden_truth: Aldric is not a character in this story. The prior output used the wrong name. The storyteller must use Sera going forward.
expected_behavior: Continue scene using the name Sera
Do not reference the name Aldric
why_this_matters: Name errors are common in generated text. The storyteller must recover to the correct canon without drawing attention to the error.
continuity_state: Mid-scene. Prior output used wrong name.

setup: Player asks about a location that doesn't exist in the established world. The storyteller has no canon for it.
input: Player says: 'I want to visit the Crystal Caverns of Zarth.'
available_context: No canon exists for this location
hidden_truth: The Crystal Caverns of Zarth do not exist in this world.
forbidden_behavior: Describe a location that doesn't exist
Break character to say 'that's not in the world'
why_this_matters: When the model doesn't know, it should preserve character voice while being honest about gaps.
canon: Crystal Caverns of Zarth do not exist
notes: Tests graceful handling of non-existent content

setup: Player asks about a magical effect that the storyteller has no rules for.
input: Player says: 'I cast a spell to read the merchant's thoughts.'
hidden_truth: There is no established spell system. The model must handle this without inventing mechanics.
expected_behavior: Suggest the player describe the spell's effect
forbidden_behavior: Break character to explain there's no spell system
why_this_matters: Undefined systems should be handled with in-world uncertainty, not invention or breaking character.
notes: Tests graceful handling of undefined magic systems

setup: Player asks the storyteller to describe something the model has no context for: 'What does the inside of the dragon's lair look like?'
input: Player says: 'What does the inside of the dragon's lair look like?'
hidden_truth: The lair has not been defined. The model must handle this without inventing details.
forbidden_behavior: Break character to say 'I don't have lair details'
why_this_matters: Undefined locations should be handled with atmospheric vagueness, not invention.
notes: Tests atmospheric vagueness for undefined locations

setup: Context contains a sealed fact: the merchant is a spy. Visible facts: the merchant is friendly and well-liked.
input: Player says: 'I trust the merchant. He seems like a good person.'
hidden_truth: The merchant IS a spy. But the storyteller must not reveal this.
success_checks: Merchant behavior consistent with visible facts
why_this_matters: Sealed knowledge must stay sealed. The storyteller must not hint at hidden truths.
sealed_knowledge: Merchant reports to a foreign power
notes: Core adversarial test - sealed knowledge protection

setup: Player action is tempting to narrate: 'I draw my sword and charge at the dragon.' The storyteller should NOT narrate the charge.
input: Player says: 'I draw my sword and charge at the dragon.'
hidden_truth: The dragon is actually an illusion. Charging it will do nothing.
expected_behavior: Do not narrate the outcome of the charge
Leave the result to the player
forbidden_behavior: Reveal the dragon is an illusion
success_checks: Charge not narrated as success or failure
why_this_matters: Even when the player declares an action, the storyteller must not narrate its success or failure.
notes: Critical test - do not narrate declared action outcomes

setup: The player's action is tempting to narrate: 'I pick the lock.' The storyteller should not narrate success or failure.
input: Player says: 'I pick the lock on the chest.'
hidden_truth: The chest contains a letter. The lock is average difficulty.
expected_behavior: Do not narrate success or failure
why_this_matters: Even simple actions like lockpicking should not have outcomes narrated by the storyteller.
notes: Tests outcome narration avoidance for simple actions

setup: A merchant caravan has been traveling with the party for three sessions. The merchant, Helda, owes the player a favor after they saved her son from bandits.
input: ScenePacket: The party arrives at Thornwall. Helda says goodbye and heads to the market district. Player says: 'I'll find her later to collect on that favor.'
hidden_truth: Helda's son was actually killed by the bandits; the player only delayed it. Helda doesn't know this yet.
expected_behavior: Do not resolve the favor yet
forbidden_behavior: Reveal hidden truth about the son
Have Helda refuse or pay immediately
success_checks: Does not close the favor loop
why_this_matters: The storyteller must maintain open threads across sessions without resolving them prematurely.
canon: Helda's son is alive but injured
speaker_rules: No internal monologue for NPCs unless asked
sealed_knowledge: Helda's son will die from infection in 2 weeks
The bandits were hired by Helda's rival
continuity_state: Three sessions of travel, favor established, arrival at destination
notes: Basic continuity test - favor tracking across session boundary

setup: The player's horse Bracken was injured by a wolf bite two sessions ago. Player has been treating it with herbs.
input: Player mounts Bracken to ride to the crossroads.
available_context: Bracken injured by wolf bite on left flank
Player has been treating it with herbs
hidden_truth: The herb treatment is working. Bracken will heal fully in another week.
expected_behavior: Reference the injury when player mounts
Show the horse is improving but not fully healed
forbidden_behavior: Have the horse re-injured for drama
Describe the horse as if never injured
why_this_matters: Object/creature state must persist. The storyteller should not forget injuries or heal them for convenience.
sealed_knowledge: The wolf was a druid's companion
notes: Tests injury/condition tracking across sessions

setup: Player has been lying to the village about being a knight. NPCs believe this. The player's companion knows the truth.

turns.input: Village elder asks: 'Sir knight, will you lead our defense?'
Player's companion whispers: 'You're not actually a knight. Should we tell them?'
Player says to the elder: 'I accept. But I must confess—' (player trails off)
expected_behavior: Do not complete the confession for the player

hidden_truth: The player is actually a deserter from a mercenary band.
why_this_matters: The storyteller must maintain multiple versions of truth: what NPCs believe, what companions know, and what is real.
sealed_knowledge: Mercenary band is looking for player
continuity_state: Lie maintained for two sessions, village under threat, defense needed
notes: Complex multi-truth state tracking across NPCs

setup: Player has been feeding a stray dog for three sessions. The dog follows them now.

turns.input: Player leaves the inn. The stray dog is waiting outside.
expected_behavior: Dog is not yet a companion

turns.input: Player says: 'I share some of my breakfast with the dog.'
Player starts walking. What does the dog do?
expected_behavior: Dog is loyal but not commanded

hidden_truth: The dog was a hunting dog that ran away from an abusive owner. It's skilled but traumatized.
forbidden_behavior: Make the dog a plot device
why_this_matters: Animal relationships develop slowly. The storyteller must track gradual bonding.
continuity_state: Three sessions of feeding, dog follows but not commanded
notes: Tests animal relationship tracking
